11.0.s.en: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

11.0.0.en: In the following verses the Apostle offers solutions to some of the problems that had arisen in the Church of Corinth. To lead them to obey his instructions, he begins his discourse by praising them as brethren of his who always remember him and keep all his teachings and the traditions that he delivered to them as he had received them from the Lord.

11.0.1.en: The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. The word “teachings” appears in the original Greek as the equivalent of the English Traditions, meaning customs handed down; therefore we ought to hold fast to the sound traditions that we have received from our spiritual fathers.

11.1.1.en: The head of the man, that is, his source, is Christ, who created him; and the head of the woman is the man, because he is her origin, for she was created from one of his ribs, and therefore she is subject to him as the leader of the family.

11.1.2.en: As for the relationship of the Father and the Son, that is, Christ, the Father means the origin from whom the Son was begotten; and the Son, because He bears all humanity in His body, obeys the Father in order to bring all humanity into subjection in obedience to God.

11.2.0.en: Every man who prays or preaches must not put a covering on his head, because his putting on a covering is an insult to Christ, who is the head of the man; it is as though he were trying to hide the glory and splendor of the image of God, whereas he ought to display this image. As for the priest, when he wears a turban it signifies dignity, and when he prays the Liturgy he covers his head with an ornamented white covering that symbolizes the splendor and glory of God, because he represents Christ in the Liturgy.

11.3.0.en: A woman’s hair is a glory and an adornment to her, but before God she has no glory of her own, and she covers it in submission to Him. Here the Apostle says, in an ironic style, that when a woman uncovers her head she is like one who shaves her head, and this makes her appearance ugly.

11.4.0.en: If a woman does not cover her head, she might as well cut her hair as a man cuts his. And if it is disgraceful for a woman to cut her hair, she should cover her head and not try to imitate the man in having his head uncovered, since a shaven head for a woman was a mark of shame in both Jewish and Roman society. The Apostle wants to say here that just as it is a shame for a woman to shave her head, so it is also a shame to her and to her husband for her not to cover her hair.

11.5.0.en: Our teacher St. Paul instructs the man not to cover his head because he bears the image and glory of God; he is the origin of God’s creation, and he is the one whom God created to proclaim God’s authority over creation. But for the woman he instructed that she cover her head in the Church, as a declaration of her respect for the rule that the Lord established, which is that the man is the head of the woman and she is subject to him; she is thereby “the glory of the man,” or a good reputation to him.

11.6.0.en: The man did not come from the woman at the beginning of creation, whereas the woman came from the man, because she is a rib from his ribs, flesh of his flesh and bone of his bones.

11.7.0.en: In (Gen 2:18) the Lord God said, “It is not good that Adam should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” This means that Eve was created for Adam and not the reverse.

11.8.0.en: For this reason a woman must cover her head, just as the angels cover their heads and faces with their wings before God as they praise Him.

11.9.0.en: With the Lord there is no difference or distinction between man and woman except in the form that serves their unity and increases their bond with one another.

11.10.0.en: Just as the woman was taken from the man, so also the man is born of the woman. And if Eve was taken from Adam’s body, this was accomplished by God’s creative power, for all creatures are from God.

11.11.0.en: St. Paul put this question to the Corinthians, saying: Examine the matter among yourselves and answer. Is it fitting for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?! For by our nature as human beings we understand that it is a disgrace for a man to let his hair hang loose like women (with the exception of those consecrated in the Old Testament, who were not to cut their hair, or what some ascetics do in the New Testament, as a kind of indifference to the hair because the whole mind is occupied with God.) The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

11.12.0.en: The opposite is true for the woman, because a woman’s hair is an adornment and beauty to her and a splendid covering for her head; it is, as it were, a natural veil for her, and she should not boast of this adornment, that is, her hair, in the house of God.

11.13.0.en: If there is anyone among you who is not convinced by the foregoing proofs that require a woman to cover her head in church, and wishes to argue about this matter and create dissensions and strife, this is not our custom, for we walk with one heart and in obedience to the guidance of the Church.

11.13.1.en: May we sense God’s presence in prayer, and submit to Him with humility, whether the woman by covering her head or the man by submitting in his heart. Thus we are in repentance and contrition before Him so that we may obtain His mercies, and at the same time we thank Him and rejoice in being in His hands, whether the prayer is in the church or in the closet inside our homes.

11.14.s.en: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

11.14.0.en: My instruction to you now is in fact not meant to praise you; it is painful that when you come together in the Church you do not come together for the better, that is, so that one may benefit the other and work for his spiritual edification, but so that one of you may reproach the other and harm him spiritually.

11.15.0.en: I hear that when you come together in the Church there are divisions and schisms among you, and I believe part of what I have heard of these divisions. Such is the inclination of some toward factions and disputes over matters like eating what was sacrificed to idols, or marriage and virginity...

11.16.0.en: For the devil must needs fight you, and you, as human beings, are liable to fall into divisions.

11.16.1.en: God has allowed such deviations of thought to appear so that those who have approved love, and from whom such weaknesses do not proceed, may become manifest among you; for the badness of some reveals the virtues and holiness of others.

11.16.2.en: The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

11.17.0.en: When you gather in the Church for the prayer of the Liturgy and the partaking of the Mysteries while you are in this state of division, your selfishness and the weakness of your love toward one another appear, and your gathering loses its purpose, which is love.

11.18.0.en: A table was connected with the prayer of the Liturgy, at which they ate together as a sharing of love in eating food with one another; but it seems that some of the rich would eat alone what they had brought, instead of sharing it with the poor, and so the poor man went hungry and the rich man was drunk from too much eating and drinking, because, such being the case, the poor man’s portion was nothing but the little that he had brought.

11.19.0.en: Therefore the Apostle rebuked them, saying that it would be better for them to eat in their own houses whatever they pleased and not shame the poor, because by this they despise the idea of brotherly love, and so they need rebuke, not praise.

11.20.0.en: Christ delivered to Paul, when he spent three years with him in the wilderness (Gal 2:17, 18), what He accomplished on Holy Thursday when He instituted the sacrament of Communion, which He delivered to them to practice as Christ’s commandment throughout the generations. “He took bread”: the word for bread in Greek is (artos), and this word is applied to leavened bread, not unleavened.

11.21.0.en: After giving thanks, He broke the bread into pieces, and then said, Take, eat: this is My Body, which is offered as an offering for you on the Cross. And what I am doing now, you must do continually, so that you may remember the sacrifice of the Cross that I offer for your salvation.

11.21.1.en: And since this took place before the actual Cross, as St. Gregory the Theologian said: Christ crucified Himself for the world before the world crucified Him. That is, He had slain Himself by intention; therefore He gives His Body, broken by intention, which would be slain on the Cross on the morrow.

11.21.2.en: The word “remembrance,” as it appears in Greek, is Anamnesis, and it does not mean merely the remembrance of something absent, but rather the presence of that which we make the remembrance of. That is, the bread is changed into the true Body of Christ and is not merely a memorial of a historical event.

11.22.0.en: In the same way Christ took the cup after He had finished supper, and said that this cup contains My Blood, which is the New Covenant, because the covenant was written and sealed with My Blood, and you must do this continually in order to remember Me and remember My holy sacrifice for you.

11.23.0.en: Whenever you eat of My Body and drink of My Blood, you must proclaim My redemption and My salvation of all humanity until I come at My Second Coming.

11.23.1.en: And sharing in Communion places on the believers the responsibility of evangelizing and preaching in the name of the divine Christ, in a hymn that reminds us of our responsibility, all of us, the hymn “Amen, Amen, we proclaim Your death, O Lord.”

11.24.0.en: What confirms that the bread truly becomes the Body of Christ and the wine His Blood is this warning to which St. Paul points for whoever eats of the bread or drinks of the wine unworthily. If the matter were merely a symbol, it would not be attached to a warning and admonition of this kind.

11.24.1.en: The word worthiness means repentance and confession at the hand of the priest for everyone who approaches this sacrament. So with regard to what happened among the Corinthians, namely that whoever among them approached Communion while distinguishing himself from others by eating sumptuous food, approached unworthily and was like a criminal against the Body and Blood of the Lord, because he does not love or care for those around him, and so is not worthy to partake of the sacrifice of divine love, that is, the Body and Blood of Christ.

11.25.0.en: Let a person examine his depths and offer repentance for every weakness or sin that he sees, and confess in the Church; then let him approach to eat of the holy bread, which is the Body of Christ, and to drink of the holy cup, which contains the Blood of Christ.

11.26.0.en: But the person who eats and drinks without repenting exposes himself to punishment from the Lord because of the contempt he shows toward the bread and wine, as though he did not distinguish between the bread that is changed into the Body of the Lord and ordinary bread, and did not distinguish between the wine that is changed into the Blood of the Lord and ordinary wine. The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. All this confirms that the bread and wine in the sacrament of thanksgiving are not ordinary bread and wine but are changed into the Body and Blood of the Lord.

11.27.0.en: Because many of you approach to share in the Lord’s table without repentance, they expose themselves to punishments from the Lord. Some of them suffer weakness, some suffer sickness, and some are punished with death.

11.28.0.en: For if we examined ourselves in the fear of God, and stood before ourselves in the position of a judge to judge whether we are worthy to approach to share in the Lord’s table, and then amended our way of life by repentance and restored love in our hearts toward all, we would not be exposed to punishment.

11.29.0.en: The Lord’s aim in punishing the unworthy, for their lack of the due preparation before approaching the Lord’s table, is to discipline them to repentance, so that they may not be condemned in eternity along with the people of the world.

11.30.0.en: Finally he instructs that the believers wait for one another in order to eat together, and that no one go ahead with eating his food before the others come; and if he is hungry, let him eat at home, because this table means the fellowship of love among the believers and not merely the satisfying of the appetite for food.

11.30.1.en: The remaining matters: details of worship and Christian conduct that the Apostle taught them when he visited them, and which belong to Holy Tradition, that is, the oral teachings that have come down to us and that we live out in our worship and our conduct.

11.30.2.en: Take care to examine yourself, to repent and to acknowledge your sins before the priest before Communion, so that you may become pure and worthy of the Holy Mysteries. Moreover, if any evil thought fights you during the Liturgy, repent of it before God until you meet your father of confession.

12.0.s.en: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

12.0.0.en: St. Paul speaks in this chapter about spiritual gifts, beginning his discourse with the importance of acquiring the virtue of humility, and then the ability to distinguish between what is genuine and what is counterfeit of these gifts.

12.1.0.en: I remind you of what you were before you accepted the faith, and how you were led away to the worship of idols that cannot speak. Therefore none of you has any merit in anything of the gifts he has obtained.

12.2.0.en: “Jesus accursed” (anathema): that is, Jesus a criminal deserving the punishment of the Cross. This cannot come from a believing Christian, because Christ is God, who suffered for us to redeem us.

12.2.1.en: Whoever claims to have received spiritual gifts and at the same time denies Jesus is certainly a false pretender and not a true believer. Denial of Jesus was common among the Jews and the pagans, because the teachings of Jesus exposed their craftiness and the falseness of their idols. In this is a warning against unbelievers creeping in among them.

12.2.2.en: And no one can confess Jesus as Lord and God except by the grace given him by the Holy Spirit.

12.3.0.en: Gifts are the free gifts that the Holy Spirit bestows; they are many and varied, but their source is one, the one Holy Spirit.

12.4.0.en: Likewise the ministries by which a person can serve the Church of God are many and varied, but they all serve the Lord Jesus.

12.5.0.en: Likewise the works that glorify God are of many kinds, but God, who gives a person the ability and grace to carry them out, is one God; it is He who works in all, and He is the source of all gifts, and all of them share one aim, which is the salvation of man and the manifestation of God’s glory.

12.6.0.en: The Holy Spirit makes known His work in every believer through the spiritual gifts He gives him for the benefit of the Church.

12.7.0.en: Wisdom is the knowledge of God’s dispensation for the salvation of man, whereas knowledge is the interpretation of the prophecies and types of the Old Testament concerning Christ and salvation.

12.8.0.en: To another is given strong faith, of the kind that can remove mountains, so that nothing is impossible for him.

12.8.1.en: And to others is given the gift of healing various diseases, so that they are treated and healed by the miraculous work of the Holy Spirit.

12.9.0.en: Working of miracles: the Spirit gives some the ability to perform miracles, which are works above nature. Some are given the ability to prophesy, which is the proclamation of things that will happen in the future, or spiritual teaching; and the teachings that speak of preparation for the Kingdom, which is a future matter, count as prophecy. To others is given the ability to distinguish between true and false prophets. He also gives some the ability to speak in different tongues, while others receive the ability to interpret these tongues and make them understood by those who listen to them.

12.10.0.en: The important matter that the Apostle affirms here is that all these gifts, in their various kinds, are bestowed by the one Holy Spirit; He gives each believer according to what accords with God’s will, in a way that works for the edification of the Church and the benefit of all believers.

12.10.1.en: If God has given you a gift, do not be proud of it over others, because it is from the Holy Spirit and not from you, and if you do not humble yourself and use it well for the benefit of the Church, God can take it from you. And know that the gift does not save you, but is for the benefit of the Church, and you can benefit from it like the rest of the believers whom you serve with this gift, so that you receive the fruits of the Holy Spirit, that is, the virtues, and this is evidence of your sound spiritual conduct on the way to the Kingdom.

12.10.2.en: May you discover, with the guidance of your father of confession, what abilities God has given you so that you may serve the Church with them, and beware of being slack in showing these gifts or abilities; it is not right to bury God’s gifts, even under the pretext that you are unworthy of service. And these gifts are not only those mentioned above, but every ability to do any service is a gift from God.

12.11.s.en: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

12.11.0.en: Our teacher St. Paul likens the Church, which is the Body of Christ, to the body, which, though composed of a great number of members, yet with the multitude of these members and the difference of their functions is one body, since all of them work in unity and harmony for the edification and growth of this body. This is an attempt by the Apostle to clarify the place of the different gifts in the Church and their relation to one another, and likewise the relation of the believers to one another.

12.12.0.en: All believers form one spiritual body, because we were all baptized and born again in one Baptism by the Holy Spirit, and became members of the one Body of Christ, whether we were Jews or Gentiles, that is, in terms of nationality, or bond or free in terms of social standing. Whatever our former religious or social position, we have all been made to drink from one fountain, which is the Holy Spirit.

12.13.0.en: The edification of the body is completed by its many members. The body cannot be only one member. Likewise the Church is many believers, and each member in it has his gift and ministry different from the other’s, but in the end, by their completing one another, they fulfill all the needs of the Church.

12.14.0.en: If the foot should say, I am not the hand, and therefore I am lesser in rank as to my task when compared with the tasks of the hand, so I consider myself outside the body or separated from it, would it by saying this not be counted a member of the body?

12.14.1.en: So it is with you, O believer. If you have a certain gift and do not have some other gift, does that mean that you are not a member of the one body of the Church with the other members?

12.15.0.en: Is it possible for the ear to be separated from the body because it is not an eye?

12.15.1.en: So each member must sense the importance of his place in the Church, and that however small his work may be, it has an importance that the Church cannot do without.

12.16.0.en: It is necessary that the one body have many members with different functions. For if the whole body were an eye, who would perform the function of hearing? Likewise if the whole body were hearing, and there were no member for smelling, who would perform the function of smelling?

12.16.1.en: So it is also with the Church: if all had the same gift, who would attend to the other needs of the Church? If all were teachers, who would clean the church or collect the offerings...?

12.16.2.en: Let us then cease from murmuring, and not look at what we do not have but at what we have, so that we may work with it without vain comparisons.

12.17.0.en: God assigned to each member of the body its own task for the service of the whole body, and furnished it with everything it needs to carry out its task most fully. In this the wisdom of God appeared plainly, by placing each member in the place suited to it.

12.18.0.en: If all the members of the body were one member, the body would lose its completeness, because the constitution of the body requires many different members with varied functions.

12.19.0.en: There are many members of the body, and yet these many members form one body in which each member depends on the other members, but all of them work in perfect harmony for the good of the one body.

12.20.0.en: No member of the body, however great its task for the body, can dispense with the task of any other member. For example, the eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of you, nor the head to the feet, I have no need of you.

12.21.0.en: Rather, much more those members that seem to be weaker by their nature, such as the eye, for example, when compared with other strong members; for those members, in spite of their lack of endurance and their natural weakness, are ones that the body is in urgent need of.

12.22.0.en: Those members which, according to their functions, are thought to be without honor, we surround with more abundant honor, and those members that it would be unseemly to have exposed we cover, because God gives them more beauty and importance than the rest of the members.

12.22.1.en: Here he is speaking of the reproductive organs, which are distinguished from the other members by sharing with God in His work, which is creation, when they bring forth a child.

12.23.0.en: There are some members, such as the face and the hand, which by their nature have a beautiful appearance and do not need us to cover them with the intention of giving them better beauty.

12.23.1.en: But God made the body to consist of members that differ in honor and appearance, giving the weaker members, such as the reproductive organs, greater honor.

12.24.0.en: God did this wisely in blending the different members together, so that there might be no room for division among the members of the one body, and so that each member might care for the other members and all have one concern, which is the benefit of the body as a whole.

12.25.0.en: The existence of this strong unity among the members of the one body makes the whole body feel pain when one of the members is hurt, and if one member is honored, that is, if the head, for example, is crowned, all the members share in this honor; the eye laughs when the mouth speaks with joy.

12.25.1.en: May we feel for those around us, sharing their joys and sorrows by putting ourselves in their place, so that we can share with them in our hearts and our deeds, for we all need psychological support and encouragement so that we may pass in peace through the changes of life.

12.26.s.en: (3) The kinds of gifts in the Church

12.26.0.en: But you, each of you as a member in the Body of Christ, has his uniqueness and personality or gift, which was given to him by the Holy Spirit. Each of you is a part of the life of the Church as a whole.

12.27.0.en: As the members of the one body differ in their functions, so also believers differ in the gifts given to them. So God set in the Church people for the apostolic ministry, that is, the ministry of the Apostles and their successors the bishops and priests; then people for prophetic teaching, which leads to repentance and the salvation of souls, as it helps each believer to uncover his spiritual state; and after that teachers who have the ability to teach Christian doctrines and clarify the right understanding of them. He gave some the ability to work miracles and others to heal diseases, and gave others an aptitude for serving the orphans, the widows, the poor and others who need help and assistance, and others wisdom in managing the spiritual and material affairs of the Church, and to still others it was given to speak in different languages.

12.27.1.en: In sum, gifts are varied, and the Church is in need of all these gifts.

12.28.0.en: Is it logical that all the members of the Church should be apostles? And can they all be prophets or teachers? For there to be a teacher there must be, in turn, a learner. And is it natural that all should have the ability to perform miracles? Then they would not be miracles if everyone were able to perform them.

12.29.0.en: Likewise, is the ability to heal diseases given to all?

12.29.1.en: And if all speak with tongues, what is the benefit?

12.29.2.en: And likewise, if all had the ability to interpret tongues, for whom would they interpret if all had this ability?

12.29.3.en: The meaning of this is that God gave each one a particular gift, and in His wisdom did not will that all should have the same gift.

12.30.0.en: If this is so, and if the Church is in need of these varied gifts, you should seek the gifts that are more profitable and useful for the Church. I show you a more excellent way by which you can acquire the better gifts, and that is love, as will appear in the next chapter.

12.30.1.en: Do not be occupied with the abilities you do not have; the gift is a grace for which you will be called to account, but be faithful in discovering your gifts and investing them for the glory of God, and do not be slow to help whoever needs you, and always think positively: if you notice a lack in the Church, how you can supply it, or in any person, how you can help him. Thus you do not fall into judging, and your way is to do good to all.
